question: A line is drawn from a point P located 13 cm away from the center O of a circle with radius 5 cm. If the line is tangent to the circle, what is the length of the tangent from point P to the point of contact with the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The tangent to a circle, the radius, and the distance from the point to the center form a right-angled triangle.

The distance from the center forms the hypotenuse of this right-angled triangle.

Given the radius is 5 cm and the hypotenuse is 13 cm, we can use the common Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13).

Thus, the length of the tangent is directly 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
• O P T 13 cm 5 cm Tangent PT = ? 

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OT) = 5 cm

Distance of point P from the center O (OP) = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let PT be the tangent to the circle at point T.

⇒ A key property of circles is that the radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ ∴ ∠OTP = 90°

⇒ In right-angled triangle OTP, applying Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ (OP)² = (OT)² + (PT)²

⇒ (13)² = (5)² + (PT)²

⇒ 169 = 25 + (PT)²

⇒ (PT)² = 169 − 25

⇒ (PT)² = 144

⇒ PT = √144 = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent to a Circle

A tangent is a straight line that touches the circle at exactly one distinct point. The radius intersecting this point of contact is always perpendicular to the tangent line.

Secant-Tangent Theorem

If a tangent segment and a secant segment are drawn to a circle from an exterior point, the square of the tangent length is equal to the product of the secant segment and its external portion: PT² = PA × PB.

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of a DCT between two non-intersecting circles with radii r₁ and r₂ and distance d between their centers is calculated as √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²].

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of a TCT between two circles with radii r₁ and r₂ and a central distance d is given by the formula √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²].
